channel.title: QuotePlace — Quote of the Day
channel.description: One quote, every day, chosen deterministically from the QuotePlace collection.

item.title: Epictetus — Quote of the Day, 2026-11-11
item.description: “Men are disturbed not by things, but by the views which they take of them.” — Epictetus

item.title: Virginia Woolf — Quote of the Day, 2026-11-10
item.description: “Mrs. Dalloway said she would buy the flowers herself.” — Virginia Woolf

item.title: Margaret Laurence — Quote of the Day, 2026-11-09
item.description: “Know that although in the eternal scheme of things you are small, you are also unique and irreplaceable, as are all your fellow humans everywhere in the world.” — Margaret Laurence

item.title: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe — Quote of the Day, 2026-11-08
item.description: “Knowing is not enough; we must apply. Willing is not enough; we must do.” — Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

item.title: Alexander Pope — Quote of the Day, 2026-11-07
item.description: “A little learning is a dangerous thing.” — Alexander Pope

item.title: Winston Churchill — Quote of the Day, 2026-11-06
item.description: “Before you can inspire with emotion, you must be swamped with it yourself. Before you can move their tears, your own must flow. To convince them, you must yourself believe.” — Winston Churchill

item.title: Aristotle — Quote of the Day, 2026-11-05
item.description: “Happiness is the meaning and the purpose of life, the whole aim and end of human existence.” — Aristotle

item.title: Rumi — Quote of the Day, 2026-11-04
item.description: “Don't grieve. Anything you lose comes round in another form.” — Rumi
